jobs.description:
Job Title:
         Southeast Greenway Project Coordinator (2 Year Term Limited)                                                      
Reports to:
     Director of Community Engagement and Education

Want to play your part in protecting our local communities from the impacts of climate change? Ready to roll up your sleeves to help achieve tangible results? Want to be part of a talented, deeply committed, and national award-winning conservation organization? Then please read on!

SLT serves a diverse audience with broad cultural heritages, socioeconomic backgrounds, genders, and orientations. We encourage applications from candidates who reflect and value the audiences and populations we serve.

Overview

The Southeast Greenway Project Coordinator supports the successful planning and development of the Southeast Greenway by supporting the Park Master Plan process, providing administrative support, and managing the systems needed for effective public/private partnerships. Working closely with Sonoma Land Trust staff, Southeast Greenway Volunteers, and the City of Santa Rosa, the Project Coordinator will provide administrative support, track progress and deliverables, manage logistics, and help keep complex work moving forward by directly supporting the team.  

Primary Responsibilities

Project Management
Coordinate scheduling, communication, and workflow among the Sonoma Land Trust staff, Southeast Greenway volunteers, consultants, and City of Santa Rosa staff.
Prepare meeting agendas and materials; document discussions, decisions, action items, and responsibilities.
Manage logistics for community engagement activities, including partner meetings, workshops, public events, outreach coordination, materials, and participation records.
Prepare timely project updates, briefings, presentations, and reports for organizational leadership, donors, the City, volunteers, and other partners.
Monitor project progress, address needs, and promptly escalate issues requiring strategic, contractual, financial, or organizational decisions.
Participate in partner meetings and public settings as assigned, providing project information and coordination support.

Administrative Support
Manage calendars, meeting scheduling, invitations, room and virtual meeting logistics, materials, correspondence, and follow-up for Greenway-related work.
Support meeting preparation and administration for project leadership, working groups, partner meetings, community engagement activities, and volunteer committees.
Process and track invoices, expenses, contracts, purchase requests, and related documentation.
Draft and organize correspondence, reports, presentations, meeting materials, and other project documents.
Support contract, grant, board, volunteer, and event administration, including tracking deadlines and compiling information for reporting and stewardship.
Respond to routine inquiries, route requests to the appropriate staff or partner, and maintain clear and timely communication across the project.
Provide logistical support for meetings, site visits, public events, donor activities, and other Greenway programs.

Systems Management
Administer project management software and shared tools used to organize work.
Develop and maintain clear file management, naming, version-control, retention, and document-access practices for Greenway records.
Maintain accurate contact databases, distribution lists, partner records, and participation information.
Develop, document, and update standard operating procedures, templates, workflows, checklists, and other tools that support consistent and efficient project administration.
Maintain integrated calendars, project work plans, reporting schedules, and deadline-tracking systems.
Train and support staff, volunteers, and project partners in the appropriate use of shared systems and tools.

Essential Qualifications

2+ years of relevant experience in nonprofit operations, project management, or executive assistance.
High attention to detail, accuracy, responsiveness, and follow-through.
Strong organizational and project coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple schedules, deadlines, details, and relationships simultaneously.
Demonstrated ability to build, manage, and improve operational systems and software, including project management, file management, database, calendar, and tracking tools.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear meeting records, correspondence, reports, and presentations.
Commitment to equity, environmental sustainability, and inclusive community-building.
Proficiency with computer operations, specifically Microsoft Office Word and Excel, Box and Google Drive in a Windows environment, and familiarity with internet use and video conferencing platforms.
Access to reliable transportation and a valid California driver's license.
Ability to work weekends and evenings.
Ability to work remotely.

Preferred Skills and Experience

SLT is open to candidates with diverse backgrounds, experience, and transferrable skills. We are looking for candidates with the following experience OR the ability to develop skills in each of these categories:
Written and verbal bilingual fluency in Spanish/English strongly preferred.
Experience supporting complex, multi-partner projects involving public agencies, consultants, community organizations, or volunteers.
Experience with public planning, park development, community engagement, urban planning, land conservation, or environmental programs.

Schedule, Salary & Benefits

This is a 2 year term limited, full-time, 40 hours per week, non-exempt status (overtime eligible) position. Hourly wage starting at $38 per hour, commensurate with experience. This position has a regular working schedule that may include evenings and weekends. The Sonoma Land Trust office is in Santa Rosa, California. Staff are working in a hybrid model, but some field work may be required.

Sonoma Land Trust’s benefits include:
Paid time off including paid vacation based on tenure, 15 paid holidays, and paid sick and family leave
100% of employee premiums for medical, dental, and vision, and 75% of dependent premiums
5% employer contribution to retirement plan after one year of employment
Employee life and disability insurance
Pre-tax dependent care coverage plans for dependent or elder care
An employee assistance program for mental health, coaching, and financial or legal consultation services
A lifestyle account annual stipend for wellness or gear purchases

About Sonoma Land Trust

Sonoma Land Trust works in alliance with nature to conserve and restore the integrity of the land, with a focus on climate resiliency. The organization is also committed to ensuring more equitable access to the outdoors. Since 1976, the non-profit Land Trust has protected over 60,000 acres of scenic, natural, agricultural and open land for future generations. Sonoma Land Trust is accredited by the Land Trust Accreditation Commission and was the recipient of the 2019 Land Trust Alliance Award of Excellence. For more information, please visit the Sonoma Land Trust website.

We are passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable working environment that is representative of the communities we serve. We know that having varied perspectives leads to better outcomes to solve the complex problems of conservation, climate change and environmental justice in Sonoma County. And to best serve the people of our community, we are taking the actions outlined in our Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Plan.

To Apply

Please submit your application through the BambooHR platform linked here. Your application should include a resume and a cover letter. If you have any issues or questions about the application or to request an accommodation, please email: staffing@sonomalandtrust.org

Sonoma Land Trust is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We strive to create a diverse and inclusive organization and encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, national or regional origins, sexes, ages, disability status, sexual orientations, gender identities, military or veteran status or other status protected by law.

Brief Description

Join Forest Lawn’s Architecture & Engineering team and play a hands-on role in shaping and maintaining the spaces that serve generations of families. The Field Survey Technician supports surveying, development, and construction projects across Forest Lawn’s memorial parks, helping transform field conditions and survey data into accurate information that guides the planning and development of our properties.

Working alongside experienced engineering and surveying professionals and under the direction of a Licensed Professional Land Surveyor, you’ll gain valuable experience through site surveys, construction layout, as-built documentation, field measurements, and other surveying activities. This is an opportunity to build your technical skills, work in a unique and meaningful environment, and contribute to projects that have a lasting impact across Forest Lawn’s properties.

What You'll Be Doing

Under the direction of the Licensed Professional Land Surveyor, perform daily field surveying operations around the memorial parks, including but not limited to: detailed site surveys to determine existing site conditions, construction staking, as-builting of installed features (walls, flatwork, utilities, etc.).
Operate GPS, Trimble Total stations, and Auto-levels to measure angles, distances, and elevations.
Perform field calculations and measurements.
Coordinate with office staff to input information sent and export collected field data to staff.
Keep survey vehicle supplied with appropriate survey materials.
Communicate effectively with the Licensed Professional Land Surveyor, office staff, contractors, and other personnel encountered during field operations.
Maintain accurate field notes, record measurements, and documentation.
Operate Forest Lawn vehicles, survey equipment, and other equipment in a safe and responsible manner at all times.

Requirements

Minimum of 1+ years of field surveying experience.
High school diploma or GED required.
Valid California Driver’s License, including state required levels of active auto insurance.
Certification as LSIT desired.
Experience with Trimble Total Stations.
Experience with GNSS receivers.
Degree from accredited land surveying or related program desired.
Knowledge of AutoCAD, Civil 3D desired.

Competitive Benefits

E-Verify is not used as a tool to pre-screen candidates.

For up-to-date information on E-Verify, go to https://www.e-verify.gov/employees/e-verify-overview.

jobs.description:
Job description:

About the Role
We are looking for a highly analytical Data Analyst to help drive product and business decisions through data. In this role, you will work closely with product managers, game designers, operations teams, and engineers to analyze player behavior, evaluate game performance, and identify opportunities to improve engagement, retention, monetization, and overall player experience.
You will be responsible for transforming large-scale player and game data into actionable insights, designing and evaluating experiments, building scalable analytics solutions, and supporting strategic decision-making across game operations and product development.
We're looking for someone with strong statistical thinking, hands-on experience working with large datasets, solid Python skills, and a deep understanding of game analytics and product metrics. Fluency in Chinese is required, and you must be able to work on-site in Irvine, CA.
Responsibilities
Product Analytics & Business Insights
Analyze player behavior, engagement, retention, monetization, and lifecycle metrics to identify opportunities for product improvement.
Partner closely with Product Managers, Game Designers, and Operations teams to define key business questions and provide data-driven recommendations.
Develop KPI frameworks and performance measurement systems to evaluate product health and business performance.
Conduct deep-dive analyses on player segments, conversion funnels, feature adoption, monetization behavior, and user journeys.
Translate ambiguous business problems into structured analytical approaches and actionable insights.

Game Analytics & Operations Support
Monitor and evaluate game performance across retention, engagement, progression, monetization, and player experience metrics.
Analyze the effectiveness of game events, feature launches, promotions, reward systems, and live operations initiatives.
Identify trends, anomalies, risks, and opportunities through player behavior analysis.
Collaborate with game designers and product teams to evaluate gameplay systems, progression systems, game economy, and feature performance.
Support game launches, content updates, and post-release performance reviews through datadriven analysis.

Experimentation & Statistical Analysis
Design, execute, and evaluate A/B tests and controlled experiments.
Define experiment frameworks, success metrics, sample size requirements, and statistical validation methodologies.
Apply hypothesis testing, statistical inference, and causal thinking to measure product impact accurately.
Ensure experiment conclusions are statistically sound and actionable for business stakeholders.
Clearly communicate experiment results and recommendations to both technical and nontechnical audiences.

Large-Scale Data Processing & Analytics Engineering
Work with large-scale datasets generated from player activity, gameplay events, transactions, and operational systems.
Develop scalable analytical workflows using Python and SQL.
Utilize distributed data processing frameworks such as PySpark to efficiently process highvolume datasets.
Collaborate with Data Engineering teams to improve data quality, event tracking, and analytics infrastructure.
Validate data integrity, identify tracking issues, and proactively improve data reliability.

Reporting & Decision Support
Build dashboards, reports, and monitoring systems to support product and operational decisionmaking.
Develop automated reporting solutions to improve analytical efficiency and visibility.
Create clear visualizations and presentations that communicate key findings and recommendations.
Deliver actionable insights that influence product strategy, game design, and business priorities.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.
3+ years of experience in Data Analytics, Product Analytics, Business Analytics, or a related role.
Strong proficiency in Python for data analysis, automation, and exploratory data analysis.
Strong SQL skills with experience querying and analyzing large-scale datasets.
Experience working with big data technologies and distributed processing frameworks, preferably PySpark.
Strong understanding of statistics, probability, hypothesis testing, and experimental design.
Hands-on experience designing, executing, and evaluating A/B tests.
Strong analytical problem-solving skills and the ability to derive actionable insights from complex datasets.
Experience building dashboards and visualizations using tools such as Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or similar platforms.
Strong understanding of product metrics and data-driven product development.
Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Fluency in Chinese (Required).
Must be able to work on-site in Irvine, CA 92618.

Preferred / Nice to Have
Experience in gaming, mobile applications, consumer products, or online platforms.
Strong understanding of game analytics, player behavior analysis, retention analysis, engagement analysis, and monetization metrics.
Experience conducting cohort analysis, funnel analysis, segmentation analysis, and lifetime value (LTV) analysis.
Familiarity with game operations, live events, player progression systems, and feature performance evaluation.
Experience working with event-tracking systems and large-scale behavioral datasets.
Knowledge of causal inference methodologies and advanced experimentation techniques.
Experience applying machine learning techniques to business or product analytics problems.
Familiarity with AWS, Databricks, Snowflake, Airflow, or other modern analytics platforms.
Experience supporting product strategy, feature development, and operational decision-making through data.
Passion for gaming and strong curiosity about player behavior and product optimization.

Who We Are

Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. The campus has produced five Nobel laureates and is known for its academic achievement, premier research, innovation and anteater mascot. Led by Chancellor Howard Gillman, UC Irvine has more than 36,000 students and offers 224 degree programs. It’s located in one of the world’s safest and most economically vibrant communities and is Orange County’s second-largest employer, contributing $7 billion annually to the local economy and $8 billion statewide.

To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

Cal-Bridge is a state-funded initiative to increase the participation of underrepresented groups in STEM doctoral education and professional careers, particularly the professoriate. The Cal-Bridge network is a grass-roots collaboration of over 200 faculty from all nine general-purpose UC campuses, 22 CSU campuses, and numerous California Community Colleges. Cal-Bridge currently operates in three disciplinary areas: Physics & Astronomy, Computer Science, and Mathematics, and hopes to incorporate two more disciplines within the next few years. Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a geologist to drive innovation in metallurgical processing to support domestic critical materials production. FETCH a Cure is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization dedicated to improving quality of life by connecting people and pets through accessible, compassionate treatment and education. Through events, campaigns, and fundraisers, FETCH promotes long, healthy lives for pets and raises awareness about pet cancer prevention, detection, treatment, and senior pet care. The Companions in Crisis program provides financial aid to families who cannot afford life-saving cancer treatments for their pets, and FETCH continues to expand access to veterinary care within the community. Through the Pixie’s Pen Pals program, FETCH supports rescue dogs and inmates in Virginia correctional centers, fostering responsibility and life skills for participants while helping trained dogs find permanent homes.

About the Program
Partnering with the Virginia Department of Corrections, FETCH a Cure’s Pixie’s Pen Pals places homeless dogs from local animal shelters in the care of men and women incarcerated at Virginia correctional centers. With the guidance of professional trainers, inmates in the Pen Pals program serve as “Handlers” to train, socialize, and provide around-the-clock care for rescue dogs in preparation for adoption — all from within the prison. We transfer an average of 80 dogs/year from shelters around Virginia. The dogs are trained and housed in the prison for a minimum of 8 weeks before “graduating” and moving into their loving adoptive homes!

Role Description
The Pixie’s Pen Pals Program Coordinator is a full-time, on-site role based in Richmond, VA. This position oversees the daily operations of the Pixie’s Pen Pals program, including coordinating with correctional facilities, rescue partners, and adopters to ensure smooth communication and logistics. The coordinator manages dog intake and placement, training schedules, and adoption processes, maintaining accurate records and program documentation. The role includes organizing site visits, monitoring program outcomes, and addressing participant and partner needs promptly and professionally. The coordinator also supports outreach efforts, and assists with events and campaigns that highlight the program.

Through events, campaigns, and fundraisers, FETCH promotes long, healthy lives for pets and raises awareness about pet cancer prevention, detection, treatment, and senior pet care. The Companions in Crisis program provides financial aid to families who cannot afford life-saving cancer treatments for their pets, and FETCH continues to expand access to veterinary care within the community. Through the Pixie’s Pen Pals program, FETCH supports rescue dogs and inmates in Virginia correctional centers, fostering responsibility and life skills for participants while helping trained dogs find permanent homes.

About the Program
Partnering with the Virginia Department of Corrections, FETCH a Cure’s Pixie’s Pen Pals places homeless dogs from local animal shelters in the care of men and women incarcerated at Virginia correctional centers. With the guidance of professional trainers, inmates in the Pen Pals program serve as “Handlers” to train, socialize, and provide around-the-clock care for rescue dogs in preparation for adoption — all from within the prison. We transfer an average of 80 dogs/year from shelters around Virginia. The dogs are trained and housed in the prison for a minimum of 8 weeks before “graduating” and moving into their loving adoptive homes!

Role Description
The Pixie’s Pen Pals Program Coordinator is a full-time, on-site role based in Richmond, VA. This position oversees the daily operations of the Pixie’s Pen Pals program, including coordinating with correctional facilities, rescue partners, and adopters to ensure smooth communication and logistics. The coordinator manages dog intake and placement, training schedules, and adoption processes, maintaining accurate records and program documentation. The coordinator also supports outreach efforts, and assists with events and campaigns that highlight the program.

Position Summary

The Specialized Programs Coordinator provides district-level leadership, coordination, supervision, and support for specialized programs and services that address the unique educational, communication, physical, sensory, nutritional, technological, and access needs of students with disabilities. The coordinator oversees assigned specialized staff and programs, collaborates with schools and district departments, supports compliance and program quality, and provides professional development and technical assistance to staff.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Specialized Program Leadership

Provide leadership and coordination for specialized programs and services across the district.
Oversee assigned specialized staff and services, including Visual Impairment (VI), Deaf/Hard of Hearing (DHH), educational interpreters, Adapted Physical Education, music therapy, assistive technology, and other specialized programs.
Monitor program implementation and service delivery and make recommendations for improvement.
Collaborate with school administrators, EC staff, families, related service providers, and district departments to address student needs.
Assist with staffing, budgeting, purchasing, resource allocation, and program planning related to specialized services.

Specialized Services

Coordinate VI and DHH services and support staff serving students with sensory disabilities.
Coordinate educational interpreter services and communication supports.
Oversee specialized meal-time programs in collaboration with School Nutrition Services, schools, families, and appropriate staff to address feeding, positioning, safety, and other unique student needs.
Coordinate special transportation needs in collaboration with the Transportation Department, including facilitating monthly coordination meetings to address student needs, concerns, equipment, safety, and service delivery.
Provide leadership and support for Adapted Physical Education and music therapy programs and staff.
Coordinate assistive technology and specialized equipment, including acquisition, implementation, inventory, maintenance, and staff training.
Serve as a district resource for schools regarding specialized equipment, accommodations, accessibility, and student supports.

Professional Development and Technical Assistance

Develop and provide professional development for teachers, teacher assistants, administrators, related service providers, specialized staff, and other school personnel.
Provide training and technical assistance related to VI, DHH, interpreting, specialized meal-time programs, transportation, adapted physical education, music therapy, assistive technology, specialized equipment, accessibility, accommodations, and inclusive practices.
Provide ongoing consultation, coaching, and problem-solving support to school-based staff.
Identify professional development needs and coordinate training based on student needs, staff needs, compliance requirements, and best practices.

Compliance and Program Monitoring

Support compliance with federal, state, and local requirements related to specialized programs and services.
Monitor services and programs for alignment with student IEPs, district procedures, and applicable regulations.
Maintain appropriate documentation and records related to specialized programs, staffing, equipment, and professional development.
Assist the Director of Exceptional Children with program evaluation, reporting, audits, and compliance activities.
Stay current with laws, regulations, research, and best practices related to specialized programming.

Collaboration and Communication

Serve as a liaison between the Exceptional Children Department, schools, families, and district departments regarding specialized programs and student needs.
Establish effective working relationships with school and district personnel to ensure coordinated services and supports.
Participate in meetings, planning activities, and district initiatives related to specialized programming, accessibility, inclusion, and student safety.
Assist the Director of Exceptional Children with special projects and other responsibilities as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge of special education and the educational needs of students with disabilities.
Knowledge of specialized programs, assistive technology, adaptive equipment, accessibility, and accommodations.
Strong organizational, communication, collaboration, leadership, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to coordinate multiple programs, personnel, and projects across multiple school sites.
Ability to provide effective professional development, coaching, and technical assistance.
Ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with school personnel, families, and community partners.
Commitment to equitable access, inclusion, and high-quality educational opportunities for students with disabilities.
